clue.text: Gather meaning is "take on again"

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a crop
the point of something is its meaning

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry claims that the word 'gather' means to take on again.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the clue look like a definition of 'gather'; in fact 'Gather' and 'meaning' are two pieces put side by side, and 'is' only joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappoint someone is to give them the same job once more, hiring them anew.

clue.text: Descartes offered work's first to continue

parts.note: René Descartes, the French philosopher, gives his first name

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word work's

explanation.surface: The philosopher Descartes put forward his first work so that he could carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew a subscription or contract is to continue it for a further term.

clue.text: One rocketed to stardom?

parts.note: read literally, this is someone fired up on a rocket towards the stars, not a celebrity whose career took off

explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller is literally launched by rocket towards the stars, which the showbiz idiom disguises.

clue.text: Ill with a pain? To put right, this should lessen it

indicators.note: putting something right means rearranging it into proper order, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A sufferer asks whether an illness and its pain can be fixed, and is told this treatment will ease it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right' sounds like a cure but is the anagram signal: ILL, A PAIN and TO are rearranged. 'with' just joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Palliative care relieves symptoms without curing, so palliation is what eases a pain.

clue.text: Perception evident for one second amid blackness

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: amid means the letters for one and second go in the middle of the word for blackness

parts.note: night is the time of blackness

explanation.surface: Perception became evident for a single second in the middle of total darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes inside NIGHT after its N; 'evident' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is the power of seeing into a situation clearly, a kind of perception or discernment.

clue.text: Asian can set about Greek character

indicators.note: set about means the word for can is placed around the Greek letter

parts.note: a tin is a can
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An Asian person is able to start work on a Greek character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb meaning 'able to', but it is the noun, a container; 'set about' wraps it round the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tibetan is a person from Tibet, a region of Asia, so is an Asian.

clue.text: Supporting member, walk with confidence

definitions.meaning: a structural bar that braces a framework is a supporting member
to swagger along proudly, chest out

explanation.definitionFit: A strut is both a brace in a structure and, as a verb, a swaggering walk.

clue.text: Lose footing as lager brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word for lager is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Pils is short for Pilsner, a pale lager

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing as the lager they drank comes back up.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip is to lose one's footing, sliding by accident on a slick surface.

clue.text: Way of beating drug

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat, a beating
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a method of beating drug addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or path from one place to another.

clue.text: Conversation involving five articles, four heartless

indicators.note: four heartless means four of those words lose their middle letter

parts.note: five articles: the definite article four times and the indefinite once, in the order THE THE A THE THE

explanation.surface: A chat that touches on five articles, four of them unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'four heartless' strips the middle H from each of the four THEs, leaving TE TE A TE TE; 'involving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people, French for head to head.

clue.text: Some scorn at a lack of delivery

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is scornful of a failure to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, and a delivery is the birth of a baby.

clue.text: It's not one's real name, so throw it on the barbie!

parts.note: taken as written
a briquet (briquette) is a block of fuel thrown on a barbecue, Australian slang barbie

explanation.surface: An Australian says a nickname is worthless, so it may as well go on the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw it on the barbie' is a cryptic description of BRIQUET, a variant spelling of briquette, a block of compressed charcoal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a nickname, a name someone goes by that is not their real one.

clue.text: Ruined, owing, yet I'm a statesman

indicators.note: ruined suggests these words are wrecked and rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician laments being bankrupt, in debt, yet still a statesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' is a pun: not a politician but a native of a US state, here Wyoming.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wyomingite is a resident of Wyoming, so punningly a 'state's man'.

clue.text: A stone turned over that's huge

indicators.note: turned over means the whole sequence of a and the word for stone is read backwards

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Someone turns over a stone and finds something enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses A plus GEM together, not GEM alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for huge or enormous.

clue.text: Sea creature mangling flesh it having slashed first

indicators.note: first places the word for slashed ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: slashed means cut

indicators.note: mangling suggests the letters are mutilated and jumbled

explanation.surface: A sea creature mauls flesh after slicing it open first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mangling' rearranges FLESH IT into TLEFISH; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish is a marine mollusc related to squid, a sea creature.

clue.text: Flier turning tail in place of rest

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters go inside the word for place of rest

parts.note: a cot is a small bed, a place of rest

indicators.note: turning signals that the letters of tail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird turns its tail while settled in its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an aviator, but it is a small bird; 'turning' shuffles the tail rather than swinging it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small European bird, so a flier.

clue.text: Dye from Indian port and ale, mixed

parts.note: Cochin (Kochi) is a port in Kerala, India

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of ale are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A dye is obtained from an Indian port mixed with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a red dye made from crushed scale insects.

clue.text: Having missed C, renounce bungling conductor

indicators.note: bungling means the letters of renounce are botched and rearranged, once the C is set aside

parts.note: C is the letter named in the clue, missed out of the anagram

explanation.surface: A conductor who blundered, having missed a note, gives up the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having missed' takes C out of RENOUNCE; 'bungling' shuffles what is left. 'conductor' is not a musician but a nerve cell carrying impulses.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurone is a nerve cell, which conducts electrical impulses through the body.

clue.text: Cricket series tense, given balance could be better

parts.note: in cricket an over is a series of six balls bowled from one end
drawn means strained or tense, as in a drawn face

explanation.surface: A tense cricket series could have been better balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' looks like part of the cricket picture, but it is a bank balance in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn account has a negative balance, so it could certainly be better.

clue.text: Feline carrier has last part of chromo some which is negative

parts.note: a cat is a feline
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

indicators.note: last part of asks for the final letter of chromosome

explanation.surface: A cat carrying a chromosome tests negative.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'chromosome' split as 'chromo some'; its last letter E ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathode is the negatively charged electrode in an electrolytic cell.

clue.text: Upstanding pose in the distance, which is for the best?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstanding means the whole built word is read from bottom to top
in means the word for pose goes inside the word for distance

parts.note: a mile is a stock distance
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Is it for the best to stand up straight and pose in the distance?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' reads as 'honest', but in a down entry it turns the whole built word to run upwards; the question mark softens a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism favours the best, giving power or privilege to a select few.

clue.text: Drastic when old lover huge not half!

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: not half means the second half of the word for huge is dropped

parts.note: tremendous means huge

explanation.surface: Things become drastic when an old flame is enormous, or rather not half as big.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' cuts TREMENDOUS to its first five letters; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme measures are drastic ones, going to the furthest limit.

clue.text: Ornate design incorporating good finishing touches

indicators.note: incorporating means the reworked letters take in the abbreviation for good
ornate suggests elaborately worked, so the letters of design are reworked

explanation.surface: An elaborate design with good finishing touches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ornate' looks like a description of the design, but it is the anagram signal, and 'incorporating' slips the good letter in among the shuffled ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgings are borders or trims added to finish off fabric or a garden bed.

clue.text: Small measure topping another

indicators.note: topping means removing the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: another small measure is a pinch, as in a pinch of salt

explanation.surface: One small measure sits on top of another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' looks like 'sitting on top of' but means cutting off the head: PINCH loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small unit of length, one twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: Noble matter

definitions.meaning: a European nobleman of a rank like an earl

explanation.definitionFit: A count is a nobleman; to count is to matter, as in 'every vote counts'.

clue.text: R for the ruling ruffian?

parts.note: R is the leading letter of the word ring, so it is the ring's leader; and a gang's ruling ruffian is its chief instigator

explanation.definitionFit: A ringleader is the person who leads a gang of troublemakers, and R heads the word ring.

clue.text: Might it be frost that is reported? Surely now the answer's sorted!

indicators.note: that is reported means the word for frost is said aloud

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A couplet asks whether frost might be in the news, then declares the puzzle solved.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue itself: 'reported' and 'sorted' end the two lines with the same sound. 'Might it be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme is a matching of end sounds, which the two halves of the clue display.

clue.text: Hussy gets cross about prostitution, finally

indicators.note: about means the word for cross goes round the last letter

parts.note: to cross breeds is to mix them

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of prostitution

explanation.surface: A loose woman gets angry about prostitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the verb MIX, as in crossbreeding; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is an impudent or flirtatious girl, an old-fashioned word for a hussy.

clue.text: Knowledge shown in programme about sport

indicators.note: about means the word for programme goes around the sport

parts.note: an edition is one instalment of a broadcast programme
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Learning is on display in a programme about sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning gained from study, a store of knowledge.

clue.text: Country where some day Latin will return?

indicators.note: will return means those letters are read backwards
some means a run of letters is taken from inside the words day Latin

explanation.surface: Where in the world will Latin one day make a comeback?
explanation.walkthrough: The run YLATI hides in 'day Latin'; 'will return' turns it round. Fittingly, Latin began in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe, the home of Latin.

clue.text: Something flexible put away following conclusion of Financial Times

indicators.note: following means the word for put away comes after that last letter
conclusion of asks for the last letter of Financial

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so ate
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: Something flexible was filed away after the end of the Financial Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Financial Times' looks like the newspaper but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex is rubbery sap or synthetic rubber, a flexible material.

clue.text: Bad luck finding mechanics with screw loose

indicators.note: a mechanism with a screw loose falls apart, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: It's bad luck to discover your mechanics have a screw loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischance is an unlucky accident or piece of bad luck.
